slides.title: Starter Activity: 6-Cell Knowledge Retrieval

starterQuestions.q: What is the purpose of blind peer review in medical journal publishing?
starterQuestions.a: Subjecting research methodology, statistics, and conclusions to independent scrutiny by field experts to detect flaws, bias, or fraud before publication.

starterQuestions.q: What distinguishes a primary research journal article from a secondary review paper?
starterQuestions.a: Primary articles present original empirical trial data; secondary reviews synthesize, critique, and meta-analyse previously published studies.

starterQuestions.q: How do you cite a journal paper with three authors in Harvard format in-text?
starterQuestions.a: (FirstAuthor et al., Year) — e.g. (Patel et al., 2024).

starterQuestions.q: Name two academic databases specialized for biomedical literature.
What Boolean operator would you use to find articles discussing both Diabetes AND Renal Failure?
starterQuestions.a: The 'AND' operator narrows search results to records containing both medical concepts.

starterQuestions.q: Why are NICE guidelines considered tier-1 clinical evidence in the UK?
starterQuestions.a: They are rigorously developed by multidisciplinary panels evaluating systematic reviews and randomized controlled trial evidence base.

courseName: OCR Level 3 Cambridge Advanced National (AAQ) in Human Biology

objectives.knowledge: Understand the hierarchy of scientific evidence: from commercial blogs and secondary reviews up to meta-analyses and RCTs.
objectives.application: Formulate advanced Boolean search syntax across PubMed and Europe PMC to source peer-reviewed medical literature.
objectives.evaluation: Critically evaluate journal papers for funding bias, sample size adequacy, and construct compliant Harvard in-text citations and bibliographies.

terminology.def: Evaluation of scientific work by independent academic experts in the same discipline before publication.
Logic terms (AND, OR, NOT) used in bibliographic search strings to combine or filter biomedical search concepts.
An author-date documentation system comprising brief in-text parenthetical citations and an alphabetized end-reference list.
Financial or personal affiliations (e.g. pharmaceutical sponsorship) that could compromise academic impartiality.
